newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia bond issues decline in May - rating firm.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia bond issues decline in May - rating firm.

text.p: The volume of bond issues declined slightly to 1.65 billion ringgit in May against 1.74 billion in April, Rating Agency Malaysia (RAM) said in its monthly report on the local capital market.
The secondary market fared worse due to an uncertain trend in domestic interest rates, the agency added.
"Bond market activities in May were largely concentrated on new issues as secondary trading activites were sidelined by the volatile interest rate environment," RAM said.
Of the new issues, Cagamas, the national mortgage corporation, accounted for 73 percent or 1.2 billion ringgit. Corporate issuers accounted for the remaining 450 million ringgit.
RAM said secondary market activity dropped sharply as interbank rates soared in the middle of May after speculative attacks on the ringgit in the foreign exchange market.
It said Bank Negara Malaysia's intervention to defend the ringgit, estimated at over $1.0 billion, caused a liquidity squeeze.
Even the maturity of a 900-million-ringgit Malaysian Government Security (MGS), or long-term government bond, did not ease the situation, RAM added.
